items.problem: Migrated `async void` event handlers that call WinRT APIs which are unsupported/throw on WinUI 3 desktop swallow the exception, producing a present-yet-dead control with no UI feedback (caps the feature at partial). Here ScenarioRegisterTask threw inside RequestAccessAsync and nothing happened.
items.evidence: migration-score.json feature 'Background activity' note: 'invoked, but produced no output/status change; newTokens 0, post-click frame did not update'; source Scenario4_BackgroundActivity.xaml.cs:68 'async private void ScenarioRegisterTask(...)' has no try/catch around the throwing await.
items.covered_at: SKILL.md ### Defensive UI for device-dependent features (lines 196-202) — currently scoped to page INIT leaving a blank window.
items.proposed_improvement: Broaden the existing Defensive-UI rule so it also covers `async void` EVENT HANDLERS (button clicks), not just page init: wrap the handler body in try/catch and route the exception to the same status/notify surface the handler updates on success, so a throwing API yields a visible message instead of a dead control.
items.generalizes: UWP samples are built almost entirely from `async void` click handlers calling WinRT APIs; on WinUI 3 desktop many of those throw (identity/device/capability gated). Requiring handler-level try/catch that surfaces errors prevents dead-control regressions across essentially every migrated scenario.
